set.body:
ADR 0007 uses "source" in TWO INCOMPATIBLE SENSES about the SAME migration:

  line 287  "must preserve text source compatibility"
  line 502  "Text callers retain exact UTF-16 support and a source-compatible ordinary path."
vs
  line 265  "This envelope migration is SOURCE-BREAKING for callers that read the current public
             fields directly"
  line 557  "Source-breaking field migration plus codec version."

The first pair means the TEXT NARRATIVE SOURCE keeps working. The second pair means SCALA SOURCE
CODE BREAKS. A reader planning the migration cannot tell which is meant, and the two readings
disagree about whether their code compiles.

This is our defect class in prose, and it is worse in THIS repository than it would be anywhere
else, because `StorySource`, `SourceView`, `sourceSupport` and `StoryModel`'s source fields all
exist -- "source" is the single most overloaded word we have.

Found independently by codex-storymodel-new-engineer (exact-document review of 220cbdc) and
concurred by codex-storyatlas-root, who both proposed the same replacement wording: "semantic
compatibility for existing text evidence" and "text-workflow compatibility". Both classed it as a
later docs-only cleanup.

CHIEF: doing it now rather than later. Docs-only, therefore gate-inert under rule 3, therefore zero
cost to anyone mid-gate. And "a later cleanup" is precisely how a record rots -- three separate
venues tonight reported finished work as outstanding because someone deferred a correction that
took one minute. Deferring a KNOWN ambiguity in a ratified architecture document is choosing to
create the next ghost.

Scope: lines 287 and 502 only. No architectural change. The ratified decisions are untouched.
set.title: ADR 0007 says both source-compatible and source-breaking about the same migration
